I lived with only a motorcycle for a few years and traveled the US on one a couple times. It's alright. But it does get old fast. The rain gets old. The heat in traffic gets old. The not having space to carry anything gets old. The eating on the road every day gets old. Now if you mean, just living your life and riding as transportation, it's super fun. I try to avoid going in the rain on my bike these days, but other than that, I ride it when I can. Sport bikes suck for anything further than 25-50 miles at a time. Cruisers are comfortable but some make you look like a faggot. Harley is still the king of cruiser bikes, but they have the stigma. Somewhat warranted somewhat not. Sport Touring bikes are weird for anything but long trips, but some guys love them. Cafe bikes are okay if you live close to work.

If you're serious about it, it can be legit.

Riding around in a bike instead of a car is a trade between safety and comfort on one hand, and the pleasure of riding on the other. If this dangerous, uncomfortable thing is just really what you want to do all the time because you love it, that's legit, and yeah that's kinda cool.

At first approximation, it's no different than falling in love with skiing or surfing, but when you look closer there's more to it than just that. Riding has a lower level of intensity but it's constant; you are never safe, never unaware. It's kind of like the difference between bravery and courage, you can be extra-bold for a few minutes at a time, or you can be steady about it always.

It can't help but impact your lifestyle, too. You learn to travel light, you learn to be self-reliant, you become accustomed to a higher level of flexibility. It's a good life, if you don't weaken. It gets a lot harder if you do.
